about: Traumatized Mr. Incredible puts two faces of Bob Parr side by side. On the left is his clean, cheerful Pixar render with blue eyes and a confident smile. On the right is a grainy black-and-white, almost photographic version of the same face, eyes swallowed in shadow, smile frozen into something haunted. The left panel stands for people who see a fact at face value; the right is people who know the dark backstory, the hidden cost or the grim follow-up. It turns obscure trivia, insider knowledge and lived experience into a quick reveal of who is still innocent and who is not.
origin: The right-hand image comes from a late-2020 experiment that ran Incredibles characters through a machine learning tool to make them look realistic, giving Mr. Incredible an eerie expression. The pairing later grew into long multi-stage versions that get darker with each step.
usage:
The left box goes over the cheerful Mr. Incredible and usually says "people who don't know". The right box goes over the haunted one and says "people who know". Above or in place of those, name the topic: a song, a place, a game, a job, a phrase.

It works when the topic sounds harmless but has a tragic, gross or exhausting side that only insiders recognize: a cozy-looking game with a brutal ending, an innocent-sounding job, a quiet street that floods every spring. Keep it light; the face does the heavy lifting.

aka: People Who Don't Know vs People Who Know
